title: Secondhand booksellers in UK and Ireland suspect AI firms behind ‘strange’ bulk orders

paragraphs.en: Secondhand booksellers in the UK and Ireland are reporting a flurry of bulk orders from mystery buyers, amid speculation AI companies are acquiring the tomes for their data.
paragraphs.zh: 英国和爱尔兰的二手书商报告称，出现了神秘买家大量下单购书的现象，外界猜测是 AI 公司在为训练数据收购这些书籍。

paragraphs.en: Bookshops contacted by the Guardian say they have been receiving orders from buyers in the US, Canada, continental Europe and the UK. The increase has been replicated around the world, with booksellers in the US, Australia and Europe also reporting unusual orders.
paragraphs.zh: 《卫报》联系的各书店表示，它们一直收到来自美国、加拿大、欧洲大陆和英国的买家的订单。这种增长在全球各地都在出现，美国、澳大利亚和欧洲的书商也报告了异常订单。

paragraphs.en: Stuart Manley, the co-owner of Barter Books in Alnwick, Northumberland, said the orders, which began arriving three months ago, were unusual because they did not follow the typical pattern of being grouped into themes such as sport or motoring.
paragraphs.zh: 位于诺森伯兰郡阿尼克 Barter Books 的联合店主斯图尔特·曼利说，这些订单三个月前开始出现，其反常之处在于它们不像通常那样按主题（如体育或汽车）归类。

paragraphs.en: “It’s definitely a strange combination of books,” said Manley. “Normally a book order is on a theme but this is all over the place.”
paragraphs.zh: “这绝对是一个奇怪的书单组合，”曼利说，“通常图书订单都会围绕一个主题，但这个订单杂乱无章。”

paragraphs.en: A recent order included requests for an Estonian translation of John le Carré’s The Mission Song, a copy of Anne Brontë’s Agnes Grey from a specific imprint and the October 1983 edition of Warship, a monthly magazine. Manley said he had sold “hundreds” of random books to three buyers for a total of about £4,000.
paragraphs.zh: 最近的一笔订单包括：约翰·勒卡雷《使命之歌》的爱沙尼亚语译本、安妮·勃朗特《艾格尼丝·格雷》特定出版社的版本，以及 1983 年 10 月号的月刊《战舰》。曼利说，他已向三位买家出售了“数百本”五花八门的书，总额约 4000 英镑。

paragraphs.en: Jim Shaughnessy, the owner of MW Books in Claregalway, Ireland, said his business had been receiving large, varied orders since May.
paragraphs.zh: 爱尔兰克莱尔戈尔韦 MW Books 的店主吉姆·肖内西说，自 5 月以来，他的生意一直收到大量、种类繁多的订单。

paragraphs.en: “They are sporadic, presumably machine-driven and have little in terms of thematic currency; books on agricultural implements in 18th century Africa through to biographies of 1950s racing car drivers,” he said. “Personally, I don’t see we have the right to dictate what any customer does with their purchases but it is more than curious to see what’s being selected.”
paragraphs.zh: “它们零散出现，很可能是机器驱动的，几乎没有任何主题上的关联；从 18 世纪非洲农具方面的书，到 20 世纪 50 年代赛车手的传记，”他说，“就我个人而言，我不认为我们有权规定顾客拿买到的书做什么，但看到这些被选中的书确实令人好奇。”

paragraphs.en: David Gower-Spence, the owner of BookLovers of Bath, said he had received a rush of orders between May and July for about 200 books from buyers who have also been cited by other sellers contacted by the Guardian for this article.
paragraphs.zh: 巴斯 BookLovers of Bath 的店主戴维·高尔-斯彭斯说，他在 5 月到 7 月之间收到了一大批约 200 本书的订单，买主也是《卫报》为撰写本文而联系的其他卖家提到的那些人。
